items.titleEn: Gold, silver decline as strong U.S. jobs data lifts yields on election day - Kitco PM Report
items.summaryEn: (Kitco NewsWire) - Spot gold and silver prices were lower in late U.S. trading Tuesday, as stronger-than-expected U.S. labor-market and factory orders data lifted Treasury yields and reinforced expectations for additional Federal Reserve tightening. Precious metals remained under pressure despite another decline in crude oil prices, while investors positioned for the U.S. midterm election results and assessed conflicting signals about negotiations to end the confrontation with Iran. At the time of writing, spot gold was trading near $3,924.10 an ounce, down $21.60, or 0.55%, while spot silver was trading near $49.450, down $1.076, or 2.13%, on the session. Tuesday's U.S. economic reports pointed to renewed strength in labor demand and manufacturing orders, complicating expectations that the Federal Reserve could soon end its tightening cycle. September job openings increased to 7.523 million from an upwardly revised 7.190 million in August , exceeding expectations near 7.15 million and reaching their highest level since May. Hiring remained relatively stable, while layoffs declined to approximately 1.64 million and voluntary quits increased to 3.37 million. The improvement suggests that employers continue to seek workers despite elevated borrowing costs and uncertainty surrounding economic growth. The figures reinforced the argument that labor-market conditions remain sufficiently resilient to accommodate restrictive monetary policy. September factory orders also exceeded expectations, increasing 1.8% following an upwardly revised 0.3% gain in August. Economists had anticipated an increase of approximately 1.2%. Orders were 7.2% higher than a year earlier, supported by a 28.3% increase in civilian aircraft and parts bookings, while machinery orders advanced 1.5% and computers and electronic products orders gained 0.8%. Nondefense capital goods orders excluding aircraft, a measure of business equipment investment, increased 0.6%, slightly stronger than initially estimated. The results followed Monday's October manufacturing purchasing managers' index of 55.5 , reinforcing the picture of continued factory expansion even as elevated input costs and financing conditions remain significant constraints.

items.titleEn: Super Micro stock faces earnings test as options signal 12.5% move
items.summaryEn: Buy Super Micro Computer (SMCI) shares into the print. The setup is strong: pre-announced revenue guidance (18.5–19.5B) is already above prior expectations, and options positioning shows traders leaning calls (put/call volume 0.73; calls dominate open interest). If management confirms AI server demand and holds margins, the stock can re-rate quickly from a depressed level (36% below the 52-week high). Key Risk: Margins disappoint—pricing pressure and component costs squeeze profit even if revenue beats. Buy a call spread on SMCI for Nov 6 (e.g., buy the $33 call and sell the $36.50 call). Implied move is ~12.5% either way with very high implied volatility, so you want defined upside exposure that benefits if the stock pops but avoids paying for the full volatility premium.

items.titleEn: Gold's October correction was overdone - Commerzbank
items.summaryEn: (Kitco News) - The gold market is holding support above $3,900 an ounce after seeing its worst monthly performance since the start of the year and its worst October since 2008. Although prices continue to struggle, one bank sees last month's sell-off as a potential buying opportunity, as the fundamental factors supporting higher prices remain firmly in place. In his latest precious metals commentary, Carsten Fritsch, Commodity Analyst at Commerzbank, said that gold's recent weakness appears overdone, particularly as the precious metal has become disconnected from traditional market fundamentals. "We consider the price decline in gold to be excessive and unwarranted. The arguments in favour of a rising gold price remain valid," he said.

items.titleEn: Gold demand remains near record highs as central bank buying surges 42% – WGC
items.summaryEn: (Kitco News) - The gold market continues to face significant headwinds from higher interest rates and elevated bond yields, but investment demand and stronger-than-expected central bank purchases are expected to provide important support for the precious metal through the end of the year, according to the World Gold Council. In its latest Gold Demand Trends report published Tuesday, the World Gold Council (WGC) said that total global gold demand, including over-the-counter investment, fell 1% year-over-year to 1,369 tonnes in the third quarter. The analysts added that year-to-date demand currently stands at 3,881 tonnes, virtually matching the 2025 record. At the same time, although demand volumes have edged lower, the value of gold consumption reached a record $566 billion during the first nine months of the year. Looking ahead, the WGC said it expects investment demand to increase by approximately 200 tonnes in 2026 compared to last year. Although investment demand remains a critical driver for the precious metal, the updated forecast represents a downgrade from the organization's previous estimate of 400 tonnes of annual growth.
